headline: Pinterest's new terms are live: the 30-day window to opt out of arbitration is open
tldr: Pinterest's rewritten terms and privacy policy took effect Nov 12. You have 30 days to opt out of its new arbitration clause by emailing litigation@pinterest.com.
who: Pinterest users in the U.S. and everywhere outside the EEA, Switzerland and the UK (the arbitration section doesn't apply to consumers there), and anyone who sends messages on Pinterest or posts Pins
seo_title: Pinterest terms took effect Nov 12, 2026: how to opt out of arbitration within 30 days
seo_desc: Pinterest's new Terms of Service and Privacy Policy are live as of Nov 12, 2026. Section 11 moves disputes to JAMS and consolidates mass claims before one arbitrator, with a 30-day opt-out via litigation@pinterest.com.

redline.after: You may opt out of this Section 11 within 30 days of first becoming subject to it by emailing litigation@pinterest.com with your name, account email, and a statement that you’re opting out; otherwise you agree to be bound by it.
redline.label: Terms of Service · 11(d) Right to Opt Out
redline.note: Now live. For existing users the 30 days started Nov 12.

redline.before: if 25 or more similar arbitration demands are filed within a 60-day period or with the assistance of the same law firm or group of law firms, AAA will consolidate the arbitration demands.

redline.label: Terms of Service · 11(c) Mass Filing
redline.note: AAA batches, each with its own arbitrator, become a single JAMS case.

redline.before: Improve the products and services of our family of companies and offer new features. For example, using information to train, develop and improve our technology such as our machine learning models, regardless of when Pins were posted.
redline.after: Improve the products and services of our family of companies and offer new features. For example, using information (such as Pins, regardless of when they were posted) to train, develop and improve our technology such as our machine learning models and our generative artificial intelligence models.
redline.label: Privacy Policy · How we use the info we collect
redline.note: Old Pins are named as AI training material, generative models included.

actions: To keep your right to go to court, email litigation@pinterest.com with your name, account email and a statement that you're opting out of Section 11
Send it by December 12, 2026 (30 days from Nov 12, our count) and keep the sent copy
what:
Pinterest's rewritten Terms of Service and Privacy Policy, first posted as previews around September 1 and covered here on October 20, are now the live versions. Our Nov 13 snapshot of policy.pinterest.com shows the "We're updating our Terms of Service, effective <DATE>" banner gone and the new Section 11 in its place. Pinterest's help page says "changes are effective November 12, 2026" and "By continuing to use Pinterest after November 12, 2026, you accept the updates to the Terms."

## Change 1: The new arbitration section is in force

For everyone outside the EEA, Switzerland and the UK, disputes now go to "binding, individual arbitration administered by JAMS" instead of the American Arbitration Association. The section "applies to any Claim you have not filed in court or in arbitration before the date you agreed to these Terms, and supersedes and amends any prior arbitration agreement between you and Pinterest, including as to Claims that arose before this or any prior arbitration agreement."

Mass claims are handled differently. The old terms sent 25 or more similar demands to AAA batches with "one arbitrator to resolve each batch." The live text says that if 25 or more claimants file similar claims within 90 days or through coordinated lawyers, "all of those Claims will be consolidated into one arbitration before one arbitrator," and the arbitrator may split fees with a claimant's lawyers or funders.

## Change 2: The 30-day opt-out clock has started

The live Section 11 says: "You may opt out of this Section 11 within 30 days of first becoming subject to it by emailing litigation@pinterest.com with your name, account email, and a statement that you're opting out; otherwise you agree to be bound by it." The old terms had no opt-out. For existing users the new terms took effect November 12, so by our count the window runs to December 12, 2026. Pinterest doesn't print that end date.

## Change 3: The privacy policy now says more about AI and message scanning

The live Privacy Policy says Pinterest uses information "(such as Pins, regardless of when they were posted) to train, develop and improve our technology such as our machine learning models and our generative artificial intelligence models." It adds "voice transcripts" to the activity used "to make inferences about you and your preferences," and says Pinterest "may also use, or work with vendors who use automated tools to scan and analyze your messages to detect harmful or unlawful content." It also says connected TVs and other devices "that use our Services" generate log data, and that "Your connected TV may allow you to manage or limit the use of data for advertising."

One difference from our October 20 write-up: two sentences we quoted from the September preview, about seeing ads "when you're streaming a show on your connected TV" and "associating devices that may relate to the same person or household," do not appear in the privacy policy text we captured on November 13. We can't tell from our snapshot whether Pinterest dropped them or moved them to another page.

Other changes: the terms add Pinterest's "GenAI Acceptable Use Guidelines" to the policies you agree to; users outside the EEA, Switzerland and the UK are told their "acceptance of these Terms constitutes your consent to the processing activities described in our Privacy Policy"; and watching YouTube content on Pinterest binds you to YouTube's Terms of Service.

What you can do: to keep your right to sue in court, email litigation@pinterest.com with your name, your account email and a statement that you're opting out of Section 11. Keep the sent copy.
sources: Pinterest Help: Changes to our policies
faq: When did Pinterest's new terms take effect?
November 12, 2026, according to Pinterest's help page. Our snapshot of November 13 shows the new Section 11 live on policy.pinterest.com.
How do I opt out of Pinterest arbitration?

Email litigation@pinterest.com with your name, account email and a statement that you're opting out. Section 11 allows this "within 30 days of first becoming subject to it", which for existing users means by December 12, 2026.

headline: JetBlue makes March 18–31, 2027 peak dates for checked bags
tldr: Late-March spring break flights on JetBlue now carry peak bag fees: $5 more per prepaid bag, $10 more if you pay within 24 hours.
who: JetBlue customers who check paid bags on flights between March 18 and March 31, 2027, typically spring break travel

redline.label: Optional Services and Fees · Peak Travel Dates
redline.note: Late March was off-peak; now it's peak.

actions: If you're flying JetBlue March 18–31, 2027, prepay bags at least 24 hours before departure: at peak that saves $15 on the first bag and $10 on the second
Compare fares just before March 18 or after March 31, when off-peak bag pricing applies
what:
JetBlue's fees page has added a spring-break block to its peak checked-bag calendar. The "Peak Travel Dates" table listed March 2027 as "N/A" on November 12. On November 13 it reads "3/18-3/31". Off-peak pricing still "applies to all other travel dates."

## What that costs

Peak dates raise every paid checked bag. Within the U.S., Latin America, the Caribbean and Canada, the page lists a prepaid first bag at $50 off-peak and $55 peak, and a second bag at $70 off-peak and $75 peak. Adding back the "savings" the page shows, paying within 24 hours of departure costs $60 vs $70 for the first bag and $75 vs $85 for the second. On transatlantic flights, Main Base and EvenMore Base pay $80 vs $90 for the first bag and $115 vs $125 for the second.

Our arithmetic: a round trip with one prepaid bag each way, flying between March 18 and 31, 2027, now costs $110 in bag fees instead of $100; with one bag paid at check-in each way, $140 instead of $120.

What stays the same: the rest of the peak calendar (Feb 11–22, Apr 1–26 and the summer months) is unchanged, and the fees themselves are the ones JetBlue set for bookings made from November 3, which we covered on November 7.

headline: Temu's Dec 7 terms: reject its settlement offer in arbitration and you could pay Temu's legal fees
tldr: Temu's new US terms (Dec 7) say if you turn down its settlement offer and win less, you pay its post-offer legal costs. They also ban AI shopping agents, and the privacy policy drops a no-name-or-email ads promise.
who: Anyone in the US who shops on Temu or has a Temu account, especially anyone who might ever have a dispute over an order, refund or data, plus people who use AI agents or bots to shop.
seo_title: Temu terms Dec 7, 2026: settlement-offer fee shifting, AI agent ban, privacy changes
seo_desc: Temu's US Terms of Use and Privacy Policy change December 7, 2026: lose after rejecting a settlement offer and you pay Temu's legal costs, AI buy-for-me agents banned, an ad promise removed. How to reject by Jan 6, 2027.

redline.after: If an offer made by one party is not accepted by the other party, and the other party fails to obtain a more favorable award on the claim at issue, the other party shall pay the offering party’s costs incurred after the offer was made, including any attorney’s fees and fees paid to the arbitration provider
redline.label: Terms of Use · Section 19, Arbitration
redline.note: New: say no to Temu's offer, win less, and you cover its lawyers from that point on.

redline.after: (including but not limited to buy-for-me agents, large language model-driven bots, or any end-to-end flow that attempts to place orders without human review)
redline.label: Terms of Use · Rules and Restrictions, item 13
redline.note: AI shopping agents join the list of banned uses unless Temu allows them.

redline.before: We do not use information which on its own personally identifies you, such as your name or email address, to show you interest-based advertising.
redline.label: Privacy Policy · Advertising
redline.note: A limit on how Temu targets ads is deleted, not replaced.

actions: To keep your current arbitration terms, mail a letter saying you reject the December 7, 2026 changes to Temu's Arbitration Agreement to Whaleco Inc., 1666 Connecticut Ave NW #500, Washington, DC 20009, USA, so it arrives by January 6, 2027; include your name and the email or phone number on your account, and keep proof of mailing
If you opened your Temu account recently, check whether you're still within 30 days of first accepting the terms; if so, you can opt out of arbitration entirely by mail to the same address
Review your ad choices in the "Your Rights and Choices" section of Temu's Privacy Policy before December 7
what:
Temu has posted new US Terms of Use and a new US Privacy Policy, both marked "Effective Date: December 7, 2026." Each page now opens with a notice that the text shown "is for your reference and will become effective from December 7, 2026," with a link to the version in force today ("Last Updated: November 1, 2026"). The Wayback Machine still shows only the November 1 terms at 06:34 UTC on November 12 and the December 7 notice by 16:37 UTC the same day, so Temu posted the new versions on or about November 12. We compared both documents, sentence by sentence, with the November 1 versions on November 13, 2026. Both are agreements with Whaleco Inc., the US company behind Temu.

## Change 1: Turn down a settlement offer in arbitration and you could pay Temu's legal fees

Temu's terms already require most disputes to go to individual arbitration instead of court. The December 7 version adds an "offer" rule that isn't in the November 1 terms: "In any arbitration between you and us, either party may make a written settlement offer on a claim at any time before the arbitrator issues a final decision on the claim." An offer not accepted within 30 days "shall be deemed withdrawn." Then: "If an offer made by one party is not accepted by the other party, and the other party fails to obtain a more favorable award on the claim at issue, the other party shall pay the offering party's costs incurred after the offer was made, including any attorney's fees and fees paid to the arbitration provider, and shall not recover their own post-offer costs."

In practice, if Temu offers to settle your claim and you go on to win less than the offer (or lose), you could owe Temu's lawyer and arbitration costs from that point on. The rule works both ways on paper, but a shopper with a small claim has far more to fear from a company's legal bill than the reverse. The clause itself says it will be "limited or eliminated" where a law or court decision bars shifting those costs.

Other arbitration changes: anyone starting an arbitration must now disclose "any relationship the party requesting arbitration has with third-party litigation funders" and hand over "copies of all applicable litigation funding agreements"; "all materials and documents exchanged during the arbitration proceedings shall be kept confidential"; and the winner of a court fight over whether the required pre-arbitration steps were followed can now also recover costs incurred "in defending against an improperly commenced arbitration." Two changes help consumers: the arbitration "will be conducted in the county where you reside," and the arbitrator no longer has to be licensed "in the State of New York."

## How Temu's offer rule compares

eBay's User Agreement (in effect for existing users since June 28, 2026) has a similar rule: "any party may serve an offer in writing upon the other party to allow judgment on specified terms," and if it is turned down and the other side "fails to obtain a more favorable award," that side "shall pay the offering party's costs from the time of the offer." eBay's version doesn't mention lawyers. Temu's goes further and spells out that those costs include "any attorney's fees and fees paid to the arbitration provider." Amazon's Conditions of Use (last updated August 14, 2026, when Amazon brought back arbitration it had dropped in 2021) send most disputes to arbitration, but the version we checked has no settlement-offer rule at all.

Temu's AI-agent wording is nearly the same as eBay's, too. eBay bans "buy-for-me agents, LLM-driven bots, or any end-to-end flow that attempts to place orders without human review." Temu's Costa Rica terms (effective July 27, 2026) already had the same item 13, so the US version is catching up with wording Temu already uses in other countries.

## Change 2: AI shopping agents are banned

The list of things you may not do gets a new item (13): using any feature, "including but not limited to ordering, payments, promotions, rewards, or account management," through "any automated, programmatic, or non-human means (including but not limited to buy-for-me agents, large language model-driven bots, or any end-to-end flow that attempts to place orders without human review) where such use interferes with, circumvents, or undermines Temu's technical measures, security controls, or the intended operation of the Services, except as expressly permitted by Temu." A new item (14) bars framing or embedding "any part of the Services, including any webpage, interface, login page, or form" in another site or app. eBay (February 2026), United Airlines (November 11) and several banks have added similar AI-agent rules this year.

## Change 3: The privacy policy drops its promise not to use your name or email for ads

The November 1 privacy policy says: "We do not use information which on its own personally identifies you, such as your name or email address, to show you interest-based advertising." That sentence is gone from the December 7 version. The section is renamed from "Interest-based advertising" to "Advertising" and now says Temu and its advertising partners may use your information "to serve advertisements and to measure the performance of advertisements shown to you." Ads on Temu itself are now called "personalized advertised listings." The policy doesn't say Temu will now use names or emails for ads; it no longer says it won't.

Also removed: "The merchandise partner will not receive your payment information or device data." Added: Temu may get information from "Age verification service providers"; "advertising analytics providers" are a new data source; affiliates Temu shares data with now include "entities that are located outside the United States"; and Temu may send marketing "via your accounts on messaging applications" linked to your phone number.

## What gets better

The terms add a right to cancel: "you may cancel your order at no cost and without prior notice at any time before it is packed for shipment and obtain a refund," and you "may still return it after you receive it and obtain a refund." The sentence saying a refund "will not cover customs, taxes, or any return shipping costs" is gone from the terms (the Return and Refund Policy still governs the details). Temu can now end accounts "for any legitimate reason," not "for any reason in our discretion." Customer-service calls and chats may be recorded for "service optimization" purposes instead of "training" purposes. Creating more than one account is no longer banned outright, only when it's done to get around the terms, account limits or promotion rules.

## What you can do

Both versions of the terms say that if Temu makes a material change to the arbitration agreement, you can reject it "within thirty (30) days of such change becoming effective by writing to us at the applicable address set forth in Section 18.5." That address is Whaleco Inc., 1666 Connecticut Ave NW #500, Washington, DC 20009, USA, and notice counts "when received." If you reject the changes, the arbitration terms you first agreed to "remain in full force and effect," so the new settlement-offer rule wouldn't apply to you. By our count the 30 days end on January 6, 2027. If you already opted out of Temu arbitration in the past, both versions say Temu "will continue to honor" that. New users can still opt out of arbitration altogether within 30 days "after first accepting" it.

Coverage (checked Nov 13, 2026): searches turned up only Temu's own pages and automated document trackers (TosDiff logged a new privacy-policy snapshot on Nov 13). We found no news coverage of the settlement-offer rule, the AI-agent ban or the privacy edits.

faq: When do Temu's new terms take effect?
December 7, 2026, for the US Terms of Use and the US Privacy Policy. Until then, the November 1, 2026 versions apply.
What is Temu's new settlement-offer rule?

In an arbitration, either side can make a written settlement offer. If the other side turns it down and then doesn't get a more favorable award, it must pay the offering side's costs from the date of the offer, "including any attorney's fees and fees paid to the arbitration provider."
Can I reject Temu's new arbitration terms?

Yes. The terms let you reject a material change to the arbitration agreement within 30 days of it taking effect by writing to Whaleco Inc., 1666 Connecticut Ave NW #500, Washington, DC 20009, USA. By our count that's by January 6, 2027. Your earlier arbitration terms would then still apply.
Does Temu ban AI shopping agents?

From December 7, yes, where they interfere with or get around Temu's technical measures, security controls or the intended operation of the service: the terms name "buy-for-me agents, large language model-driven bots" and order flows "without human review," unless Temu expressly permits them.
Will Temu use my name or email for ads?

The new privacy policy doesn't say it will. It removes the old sentence saying Temu does not use information that on its own identifies you, "such as your name or email address," to show you interest-based ads.
Do other shopping sites have the same settlement-offer rule?

eBay's User Agreement has a similar rule: turn down a written offer, fail to get a more favorable award, and you pay the other side's costs from the time of the offer. Temu's version goes further by saying those costs include attorney's fees and arbitration-provider fees. Amazon's current Conditions of Use don't have a settlement-offer rule.

headline: Dec 1 shutdown: unused credits expire and do not transfer
tldr: remove.bg's website, accounts and self-service API stop on Dec 1 at 9:00 a.m. CET. Unused credits expire and are non-refundable; export invoices before then.
who: Anyone with unused remove.bg credits or a subscription, plus people who use the website, the self-service API, or the Photoshop plugin and other integrations
seo_title: remove.bg shuts down Dec 1, 2026: unused credits expire, invoices must be exported first
seo_desc: remove.bg's standalone site and self-service API close Dec 1, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. CET. Unused credits expire and are non-refundable. Annual plans get a pro-rata refund; export invoices before the shutdown.

redline.after: All credits (including pay-as-you-go (PAYG) credits, monthly rollover credits and any other type of credits) may be used until December 1 2026 only. Any unused credits will expire on that date and are non-refundable.
redline.label: General Terms and Conditions · credits (updated 9th September 2026)
redline.note: This covers PAYG and monthly rollover credits, not only pay-as-you-go.

redline.after: If you have unused time on your plan beyond that date, you'll receive a pro-rata refund to your original payment method. No action is required from you to receive this refund.
redline.label: FAQ · I have an active annual subscription. Will I receive a refund?
redline.note: Annual plans keep working until 9:00 a.m. CET on Dec 1, then end automatically.

redline.after: Any final renewal on or after 1 November is free.
redline.label: FAQ · I have an active monthly subscription. What happens?
redline.note: Monthly plans also end automatically after 9:00 a.m. CET on Dec 1.

actions: Use any remaining credits before December 1, 2026: unused credits expire that day and are non-refundable
Export your credit usage report and invoices from your remove.bg Account page before December 1; the FAQ says you won't be able to download them afterward
If you use the self-service API, follow Leonardo.Ai's migration guide before December 1 (enterprise API contracts continue as normal). Website users are pointed to Canva's Background Remover
what:
remove.bg, the background-removal tool now owned by Canva, is closing its standalone website, accounts and self-service API on December 1, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. CET. That is the time on remove.bg's own FAQ, fetched November 13, 2026. Background removal moves into Canva for everyday use, and the self-service API moves to Leonardo.Ai, which Canva also owns. Enterprise API contracts "aren't affected and continue as normal."

The facts below are from that FAQ and from remove.bg's General Terms and Conditions, which the FAQ links and which are marked "Last updated: 9th September 2026."

## Unused credits expire, and nothing transfers

The General Terms say: "All credits (including pay-as-you-go (PAYG) credits, monthly rollover credits and any other type of credits) may be used until December 1 2026 only. Any unused credits will expire on that date and are non-refundable." The FAQ's pay-as-you-go answer is shorter: "Any unused PAYG credits will expire on 1 December 2026. We recommend using your credits before the migration date."

Neither the FAQ nor the General Terms describes any transfer of unused credits, invoices or subscriptions to Canva or Leonardo.Ai. Those products are presented as replacements, not as a continuation of your remove.bg balance.

## What happens to subscriptions

Annual plans "will continue to work normally until 1 December 2026 at 9:00 a.m. CET." After that, the FAQ says, the plan "ends automatically and you won't be charged again." Unused time past that date is refunded "pro-rata" to the original payment method, and "No action is required from you to receive this refund."

Monthly plans also keep working until the same moment, then end automatically. "Any final renewal on or after 1 November is free." You can cancel earlier at [remove.bg/dashboard](https://www.remove.bg/dashboard).

## Invoices and account access

Account data stays available until 9:00 a.m. CET on December 1. After that, "the website and accounts won't be accessible." The FAQ says to export your credit usage report and invoices from your Account page before then: "You won't be able to download them afterward."

## API, plugins and what replace them

The self-service API "will stop accepting requests from 1 December 2026." remove.bg points those users to Leonardo.Ai's API and a migration guide. Enterprise contracts are unchanged.

The Photoshop plugin "won't be available after 1 December 2026." The FAQ points Photoshop users to Affinity, also part of Canva; Affinity itself is free, but its built-in background removal "runs on Canva AI, so you'll need a Canva Pro subscription to use it." Other integrations and plugins "will be discontinued on 1 December 2026."

## What to do before December 1

- Spend unused credits. The General Terms make them non-refundable after that date.
- Export invoices and your credit usage report from the Account page while you can still sign in.
- If you are on a monthly plan, the final renewal on or after November 1 is already free; cancel earlier only if you want the plan to end sooner.
- If you are on an annual plan, you do not need to file a refund request for unused time past December 1.
- Self-service API users should plan the move to Leonardo.Ai now. Website and bulk users are pointed to Canva. Photoshop users are pointed to Affinity, with the Canva Pro caveat above.
- Enterprise API customers can keep their current contracts.

Coverage (checked Nov 13, 2026): Several independent how-to sites have already written about the shutdown. This page cites only remove.bg's FAQ and General Terms.
sources: remove.bg FAQ: remove.bg is moving to Canva
remove.bg General Terms and Conditions (last updated 9th September 2026)
faq: When does remove.bg shut down?
December 1, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. CET, according to remove.bg's FAQ (fetched November 13, 2026). The standalone website, accounts and self-service API stop then.
Do unused remove.bg credits transfer to Canva or Leonardo.Ai?

No transfer is described. The General Terms (updated September 9, 2026) say all unused credits expire on December 1, 2026, and are non-refundable. The FAQ recommends using pay-as-you-go credits before that date.
Do annual subscribers get a refund?
Yes, for unused time past December 1. The FAQ says you will receive a pro-rata refund to your original payment method and that no action is required.
What happens to monthly subscriptions?
They work until 9:00 a.m. CET on December 1, then end automatically. Any final renewal on or after November 1 is free. You can cancel earlier at remove.bg/dashboard.
Can I still download invoices after December 1?
No. The FAQ says to export your credit usage report and invoices from your Account page before December 1, because you will not be able to download them afterward.

headline: cPanel raises Solo from $29.99 to $32.99 a month on Dec 16
tldr: cPanel license prices rise on Dec 16 for new orders and every renewal on or after that date. Solo goes from $29.99 to $32.99 a month; Admin, Pro, Premier and extra accounts go up as well.
who: Anyone who buys a cPanel Solo, Admin, Pro or Premier license from the cPanel Store, or whose license renews on or after December 16, 2026

seo_desc: cPanel license prices change December 16, 2026 for new orders and renewals. Solo rises from $29.99 to $32.99 a month. Admin, Pro, Premier and per-account add-ons also increase, per cPanel's pricing page and 2027 licensing guide.

redline.note: $29.99 is on the live pricing page (fetched Nov 13). $32.99 is in the Store Licensing Guide 2027, valid from December 16, 2026.

actions: If you want to renew at today's Store price, do it before December 16, 2026: the new prices apply to all renewals on or after that date
If you buy through a hosting partner rather than the cPanel Store, ask them what you will be charged; the figures below are cPanel Store prices, excluding VAT
what:
cPanel has posted a notice on its [pricing page](https://www.cpanel.net/pricing/): "effective December 16, 2026, cPanel license pricing will be adjusted, affecting new orders and all renewals on or after that date." The notice links to the [Customer Licensing Guide](https://www.cpanel.net/customer-licensing-guide/), which embeds cPanel's Store Licensing Guide 2027, marked "Valid from December 16, 2026." Both pages were fetched November 13, 2026.

The live pricing page still shows today's Store prices. The 2027 guide shows the prices that apply from December 16. All figures below are official cPanel Store prices, excluding VAT, for Cloud/VPS licenses unless noted. Partners and hosting providers may charge something different.

## The new monthly prices

| Tier | Accounts | Until Dec 15 (pricing page) | From Dec 16 (2027 guide) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Solo | 1 | $29.99 | $32.99 |
| Admin | Up to 5 | $35.99 | $38.99 |
| Pro | Up to 30 | $53.99 | $58.99 |
| Premier | Up to 100 | $69.99 | $76.99 |
| Each account above 100 | Premier only | $0.49 | $0.55 |

Solo, Admin and Pro can also be billed annually. The pricing page today lists those as $27.46, $32.96 and $49.46 a month billed annually. The 2027 guide lists annual Store totals of $362.89, $428.89 and $648.89. Premier stays monthly only, and Metal (dedicated) is offered only at the Premier price.

## When you pay the new price

The pricing-page notice is specific: the adjustment affects "new orders and all renewals on or after that date." A license that renews on December 16 or later is billed at the new rate. One that you renew before December 16 is still at today's Store price for that term.

Coverage (checked Nov 13, 2026): We are citing only cPanel's pricing page and Store Licensing Guide 2027.
sources: cPanel Store Licensing Guide 2027 (PDF, valid from December 16, 2026)
faq: When do cPanel prices go up?
December 16, 2026, for new orders and for every renewal on or after that date, according to the notice on cPanel's pricing page (fetched November 13, 2026).
How much is cPanel Solo after the increase?
The Store Licensing Guide 2027 lists cPanel Solo Cloud at $32.99 a month, up from $29.99 on the live pricing page. Annual Solo is listed at $362.89.
Do existing licenses stay at the old price?
Not past their next renewal on or after December 16. The notice says the adjustment affects all renewals on or after that date, as well as new orders.

headline: Logos and Verbum raise prices Dec 7: +$1 to $2 a month for most plans

what:
Faithlife is raising prices on English Logos and Verbum subscriptions beginning at 12:00 a.m. Pacific Time on December 7, 2026. The announcement was posted on November 2, 2026, in a [Logos Community thread](https://community.logos.com/forums/topic/239417-subscription-prices-are-changing-december-7-faq/) by Jason Stone of Logos. Matching FAQs are live on [logos.com/subscription-faq](https://www.logos.com/subscription-faq) and [verbum.com/subscription-faq](https://verbum.com/subscription-faq) (all fetched November 13, 2026).

The change covers Logos and Verbum Premium, Pro and Max. It "doesn't affect Logos Plus, Logos for Church, Logos for Education, or Logos for Ministry."

## How much it goes up

Logos says most customers will see their current rates increase by these amounts, depending on plan and billing cycle:

| | Monthly | Annually | 2-year |
|---|---|---|---|
| Premium | +$1.00 | +$10.00 | +$18.99 |
| Pro | +$1.50 | +$15.00 | +$28.49 |
| Max | +$2.00 | +$20.00 | +$37.99 |

The FAQs also state the new everyday list prices for people who still have an ownership discount: they "keep paying less than the new everyday price of $10.99/month for Premium, $16.49/month for Pro, and $21.99/month for Max." Academic discounts stay at the same percentage (the Verbum FAQ says students still get 30% off and faculty 40% off) on the new base rate. Your exact figure is on your account subscription page.

## When you are charged

The FAQs: "If you're on a monthly subscription, the new price starts with your first payment on or after 12 a.m. (PST) December 7, 2026. If you're on an annual or two-year subscription, nothing changes until your next renewal after December 7, 2026." Logos will email you 30 days before the first payment at the new price (monthly users also see it on the prior month's receipt).

A current two-year term is not cut short. When it renews, the FAQ says it "renews for a year at the new annual price," unless you buy another two-year term.

## What you can do before December 7

You can switch to annual billing before December 7 and "pay the current annual price for your next 12 months." The FAQ notes that an annual plan "costs about the same as 10 monthly payments," and a two-year plan "about the same as 19 monthly payments."

December 7 is also the last day to start earning a Legacy Fallback License. If you own a Logos or Verbum package and are not yet subscribed, you need to subscribe by then and stay subscribed for 24 months in a row. After December 7, "no one can start earning a Legacy Fallback License."

The FAQs say nothing else about the plan is changing: "You'll get the same features, books, and billing options. Only the price is changing."

Coverage (checked Nov 13, 2026): We are citing Logos's own community announcement and the Logos and Verbum subscription FAQs.
sources: Logos Community: Subscription prices are changing December 7 + FAQ (Jason Stone, Nov 2, 2026)
faq: When do Logos and Verbum prices go up?

At 12:00 a.m. Pacific Time on December 7, 2026, for the first renewal on or after that time. Monthly plans are charged the new price on that first payment; annual and two-year plans wait until their next renewal.
How much is the increase?

Logos's November 2 community post says most customers see +$1.00, +$1.50 or +$2.00 a month on Premium, Pro and Max, or +$10, +$15 or +$20 a year. The new everyday list prices in the FAQs are $10.99, $16.49 and $21.99 a month. Check your account page for your rate.
Does this affect Logos for Church or Logos Plus?
No. The community announcement says the change does not affect Logos Plus, Logos for Church, Logos for Education, or Logos for Ministry.
Can I keep today's annual price for another year?
Yes, if you switch to annual (or buy annual or two-year) before December 7, 2026. The FAQ says you will pay the current annual price for the next 12 months.

what:
discovery+'s U.S. help center has a page titled "discovery+ plan price changes," fetched November 13, 2026. It says plan prices "increased for new subscriptions in the U.S. on October 13, 2026."

"The discovery+ plan increased by $1 to $6.99/month (plus applicable taxes). The discovery+ (Ad-Free) plan increased by $2 to $11.99/month (plus applicable taxes)." By that wording, Ad-Free was $9.99 and the ad-supported plan was $5.99.

## When existing subscribers pay it

New subscribers have been charged the new prices since October 13. For current subscribers, the page says: "You'll be charged the new monthly price on your next billing date on or after November 12, 2026."

If you are billed by discovery+ or an app store, the subscription "will automatically renew at the new price (plus applicable taxes) on your first billing date on or after November 12, 2026." If you have a promotional discount, "your price won't increase until your promotional period ends."

If you are billed through another provider, such as Amazon Prime Video Channels, DIRECTV, the Roku Channel, or Sling TV, "your provider will let you know of any price changes (as applicable)."

The help center walks through how to see who bills you and when the next date is: sign in at the discovery+ app or discoveryplus.com, open Account, and read the Subscription section.

Coverage (checked Nov 13, 2026): We are citing only discovery+'s own help article.

faq: How much does discovery+ Ad-Free cost now?
The help center says the Ad-Free plan increased by $2 to $11.99 a month, plus tax. The ad-supported plan increased by $1 to $6.99 a month, plus tax.
When does the new price hit my bill?

If you are a current U.S. subscriber billed by discovery+ or an app store, on your first billing date on or after November 12, 2026. New U.S. subscribers have paid the new prices since October 13. Promotional discounts last until the promo ends.
What if Amazon or Sling bills me for discovery+?
The help center says your provider will let you know of any price changes. Check that provider's statement or subscription settings.
